title: Impact of Analyst Coverage on Firm Investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We use the Instrumental Variable (IV) method to analyze the impact of analyst coverage on firm investment decisions. The broker merger (z) serves as an instrumental variable for analyst coverage (x), allowing us to identify the causal effect of analyst coverage on firm investment (y). The key assumption is that the broker merger affects firm investment only through its impact on analyst coverage, and not through other channels. Additionally, we assume that the instrument is relevant (i.e., broker mergers lead to changes in analyst coverage) and that the instrument is exogenous (i.e., broker mergers are not correlated with unobserved factors affecting firm investment).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(plm)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s71_data.csv")

# Run the first-stage IV regression
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
summary(first_stage)

# Run the second-stage IV regression
second_stage <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
summary(second_stage)

# Run the IV regression using 2SLS
iv_model <- plm(y ~ controls | x ~ z + controls, data = data, model = "random", index = c("firm"))
summary(iv_model)

# Perform robustness checks (e.g., check for over-identification)
# Note: In this example, we only have one instrument, so we cannot perform an over-identification test.

# Calculate the coefficient of interest (the effect of analyst coverage on firm investment)
coefficient <- coef(iv_model)[2]
print(paste("The estimated effect of analyst coverage on firm investment is: ", coefficient))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient on analyst coverage to be positive, indicating that an increase in analyst coverage leads to an increase in firm investment. This is because analyst coverage can provide firms with more information and attention from investors, leading to increased investment. The magnitude of the coefficient will depend on the specific characteristics of the data, but we might expect a coefficient in the range of 0.1 to 0.5, indicating that a one-standard-deviation increase in analyst coverage leads to a 10-50% increase in firm investment. However, the actual coefficient may be smaller or larger, depending on the underlying relationships in the data.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use broker mergers as an instrument for analyst coverage.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased analyst coverage significantly boosts firm investment.
